passages.note: Senate floor Aye on final Senate passage of the amended (SAFETY Act) text; 8 of 40 voted No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text matching the Senate-amended version she voted on; operative Sec. 220.5 forbids rules requiring disclosure, and nothing in it requires staff to withhold, so it does not reach rung 1.

rows.reasoning: She voted Aye on Senate final passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), a single-subject pupil-rights bill whose operative Section 220.5 says a school district or charter school "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose" a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents." It does not reach "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents unless the student consents," because the bill only removes any duty to disclose and does not forbid disclosure.
